The new guard test only scans three files: tests/unit/test_cli_review_alias.py:336 `for rel in ("docs/llm-framework.md", "docs/cli-reference.md", "AGENTS.md"):` — so this file is not covered.
The commit updated AGENTS.md, cli-reference.md, llm-framework.md, mcp-reference.md, output-schemas.md but not llm-example-configs.md (not in the 18 changed files).
advisory.finding: docs/llm-example-configs.md still shows a live, paste-able example command `rebar review <id>` with no deprecation note, advertising the retired verb as current usage.
scenarios: An operator copies the example config guidance and scripts `rebar review <id>`, landing on a deprecated shim whose semantics diverge (fast-fail on non-claimable tickets, exit-code differences).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Update `test_cli_optionality`'s `review_ticket` argv (test_llm_optionality.py:173) to drop the positional `ticket-quality` (or wrap in `pytest.raises(SystemExit)`), since `rebar review` now rejects a positional reviewer_id with exit 2.
evidence: tests/interfaces/store/test_llm_optionality.py:173 — `"review_ticket": ["review", epic, "ticket-quality"],` passes a positional reviewer_id
tests/interfaces/store/test_llm_optionality.py:179 — `rc = main(argv)` (no `pytest.raises(SystemExit)` wrapper)
tests/interfaces/store/test_llm_optionality.py:185 — `assert rc == 1, f"{op} should exit 1 when the extra is absent"`

src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py:199-204 — `if args.reviewer_id: parser.error(f"unrecognized positional argument: {args.reviewer_id!r} — ...")` raises argparse SystemExit(2) BEFORE the agents-extra degradation path
src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py:428-432 — `main()` wraps `_main_dispatch` only in a `RemovedInputError` handler; `SystemExit` is NOT caught, so it propagates uncaught out of `main(argv)`
advisory.finding: The `rebar review` CLI verb narrows its accepted input — a positional `reviewer_id` (previously valid, e.g. `rebar review <id> ticket-quality`) is now rejected with argparse exit 2 — but the consumer `test_cli_operation_degrades_without_extra` still passes `ticket-quality` as a positional and expects exit 1, so it breaks.
scenarios: Running the `review_ticket` parametrization of `test_cli_operation_degrades_without_extra` on a clean-wheel CI lane without the [agents] extra: `rebar review <id> ticket-quality` now exits 2 (positional rejected) instead of exiting 1 with the missing-extra Error, and `main()` raises SystemExit(2) uncaught.
advisory.suggested_fix: Change the argv at test_llm_optionality.py:173 to `["review", epic]` (no positional reviewer) so the shim reaches the forwarded degradation path and exits 1, matching the parametrized assertion; or move review_ticket to a separate test asserting the exit-2 rejection.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the `rebar review --output json` shape change (review_result → plan_review_verdict) is acceptable pre-1.0 with only the documented deprecation notice, and that no packaged/repo consumer parses the old `findings[]` shape from the `review` verb.
evidence: src/rebar/schemas/__init__.py:309 — `"review": PLAN_REVIEW_VERDICT,` (was `"review": REVIEW_RESULT`)
src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py:217-222 — the shim forwards to `_review_plan`, which emits `plan_review_verdict` JSON (src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py:546-547)
docs/output-schemas.md:57 — `| \`review\` (deprecated CLI shim)   | \`plan_review_verdict\`     |` documents the repoint

review_result exposes `findings[]` (src/rebar/schemas/review_result.schema.json:5) whereas plan_review_verdict exposes `blocking`/`advisory`/`coaching` (src/rebar/llm/__init__.py:31 example `result["blocking"]`)
advisory.finding: The `rebar review --output json` wire shape changes from `review_result` to `plan_review_verdict` (OUTPUT_SCHEMAS['review'] repointed to PLAN_REVIEW_VERDICT), an unversioned change to the emitted JSON contract of an existing public CLI verb; downstream automation parsing `rebar review` JSON (expecting `findings[]`) will silently mis-parse the new `{verdict, blocking[], advisory[], coaching[], ...}` shape.
scenarios: A script or tool that runs `rebar review <id> --output json` and reads `result['findings']` now receives a plan_review_verdict dict with no top-level `findings` key.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the source-text grep in test_internal_callers_use_the_silent_impl with a behavioral assertion (invoke diff_review_paths and the eval solver's ticket-quality path under warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) and assert no DeprecationWarning is emitted).
evidence: tests/unit/test_cli_review_alias.py:273-275: `for mod in (review_workflows, eval_solver, mcp_llm):\n    src = Path(mod.__file__).read_text(encoding="utf-8")\n    assert "_review_ticket_impl" in src`
Docstring at line 266-267 claims 'Asserted on the resolved call target, not on source text' — contradicted by the body.

Refactoring violation: passes if '_review_ticket_impl' appears only in a comment/docstring while the actual call uses the warning wrapper; breaks on a behavior-preserving refactor (import alias, getattr dispatch, re-export).
Only test_mcp_tool_emits_one_signal (line 279) behaviorally asserts absence of a DeprecationWarning; it covers only the MCP tool.
search of tests for DeprecationWarning near the workflow-parity test returned no hits: tests/interfaces/store/test_review_as_workflow.py has no DeprecationWarning or filterwarnings assertion.

The diff's own message notes pytest 'has no filterwarnings key, so the warning is recorded rather than raised' — meaning an accidental switch of review_workflows/eval_solver to the warning wrapper would NOT fail existing suites.
src/rebar/llm/review_workflows.py:86 and src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_solver.py:312 call operations._review_ticket_impl — the exact call site a regression could revert.
advisory.finding: test_internal_callers_use_the_silent_impl is source-grepping: it reads each module's source text and asserts the substring '_review_ticket_impl' appears, rather than asserting behavior. Its own docstring claims it checks 'the resolved call target, not on source text', but the body does the opposite.
merged_from: The 'internal callers do not double-signal the deprecation' contract has behavioral coverage only for the MCP surface; the review_workflows (diff_review_paths) and eval_solver callers have no behavioral test asserting they emit no DeprecationWarning, so a regression routing them through the public wrapper would be undetected.
scenarios: A future edit reintroduces `operations.review_ticket(...)` in review_workflows.py or eval_solver.py while leaving the string '_review_ticket_impl' in a comment — the test still passes.
A refactor references the impl via an alias — the test breaks with no behavior change.
advisory.suggested_fix: For review_workflows and eval_solver, call the actual entry points (e.g. review_workflows.diff_review_paths(...) with a FakeRunner, and the eval solver's ticket-quality branch) inside `with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught: warnings.simplefilter('always')` and assert no DeprecationWarning was recorded — mirroring test_mcp_tool_emits_one_signal — instead of grepping module source.
